A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lagrange Large Language Models study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 6.2–6.3 report original LLaMA-7B experiments with length and helpfulness/harmlessness constraints. Figures 2–3 contain numerical outcomes, and Table 1 presents generated responses.

after.justification: The original experiments and their outcomes remain in Sections 6.2–6.3, Figures 2–3, and Table 1.

M1.justification: The constrained objective, relaxed logarithmic barrier, gradient procedure, alternating objective updates, and reward-model construction remain unchanged. Revised terminology and the efficiency discussion do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraChat instruction-following data and Helpful/Harmless preference data, with the same response-length and helpfulness/harmlessness constraint scenarios. No evaluated dataset, task, or domain is added.

E2.justification: The SFT comparator and adapted minimax (MM) method remain unchanged. Figure 3 retains the same initialization reference and the same three MM constraint settings; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendix A retain the same model, preprocessing, splits, training budgets, hyperparameters, sampling procedure, and evaluation metrics. Replacing some references to task perplexity with task objective does not establish a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: The constraint sweeps in Figures 2–3 and illustrative responses in Table 1 are retained. Neither version contains additional ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses absent from the other.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same mean-and-standard-deviation summaries and the same boxplot conventions, including 95% confidence intervals for medians. No repeated-run, seed, or statistical-testing information is added.

E6.justification: Section 6.3 corrects the MM mean-perplexity description from higher than 0.822 to greater than or equal to 0.822, matching Figure 3's existing 0.822 entries. Numerical table entries, plotted results, and generated examples otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4 corrects the inactive-constraint example from reward ≥ threshold to reward > threshold. Section 6.2 also corrects the stated threshold for the negated length reward to −l_high; its actual constraint formula was already correct. The main derivations and Appendix B remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: combine SFT and alignment through constrained optimization, solve it using logarithmic barriers, and demonstrate customizable preferences while preserving task performance.

C2.justification: Where v1 describes essentially the same time complexity as traditional approaches, v2's new Section 5.3 explicitly argues for lower memory use and faster fine-tuning through avoiding reference-model storage and evaluation. This expands the efficiency interpretation without adding resource measurements.

D1.justification: Section 6 adds a code-availability statement and repository pointer absent from v1. Hardware, implementation techniques, preprocessing, and Appendix A hyperparameters otherwise remain the same; the repository itself was not accessed.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 makes memory and evaluation-time savings explicit advantages over the approaches of Moskovitz and Dai, extending the earlier reference-model discussion. The cited-work set remains unchanged; Guo's preprint-to-publication update is bibliographic rather than new literature.

P1.justification: Sentence polishing and terminology refinements occur throughout. A short Memory and Time Complexity subsection is added, moving Implementation Details to Section 5.4, while the overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact. Publication and author-note text also change.

P2.justification: Table 1 and Figures 1–3 retain their designs and content. The conference header, author footnote, small caption and equation-spacing edits, and text reflow around Figures 2–3 produce limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: The code pointer improves access documentation, and the corrected constraint conditions and MM result description improve precision. The efficiency discussion adds useful explanation, although its stronger claims lack new timing or memory measurements. With the method and empirical evidence otherwise unchanged, the overall gain is limited.
